title: Renal Cell Carcinoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard oncology references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - the physician decides. Full pathway: workup -> presentation -> localized stage / post-nephrectomy risk / adjuvant; advanced clear-cell by IMDC risk with a line-of-therapy spine (first line -> response assessment -> second line -> response -> later line); non-clear-cell by subtype with a progression sub-step; recurrence and surveillance. Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; modalities/agents without a dose protocol (surgery, ablation, adjuvant pembrolizumab, IO+TKI combinations, single-agent nivolumab, lenvatinib, belzutifan, platinum chemotherapy) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Invents no dose/regimen/criterion. Content authored in original words; no proprietary guideline text reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison), Kidney Cancer. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers.

a.text: IMDC (International Metastatic RCC Database Consortium) risk model: 0 factors = favorable, 1-2 = intermediate, 3-6 = poor. Factors: less than 1 year from diagnosis to systemic therapy, Karnofsky PS under 80, anemia (Hgb below lower limit of normal), hypercalcemia (corrected Ca above upper limit), neutrophilia, thrombocytosis.

b.text: Adjuvant pembrolizumab for about 1 year improved disease-free (and later overall) survival in resected clear-cell RCC at increased risk of recurrence. Weigh against immune toxicity; no dedicated dose protocol here yet.

c.text: Dual checkpoint blockade (nivolumab + ipilimumab) is a category 1 first-line option for intermediate/poor-risk clear-cell disease; benefit is less established for favorable-risk, where an IO+TKI combination or TKI monotherapy are reasonable.

d.text: Non-clear-cell RCC is biologically heterogeneous; enrollment in a clinical trial is preferred where available. Data are largely extrapolated or drawn from smaller studies.

e.text: Reassess disease with cross-sectional imaging (RECIST-style) at defined intervals; separate pseudoprogression on immunotherapy from true progression before switching lines. Response or durable stable disease continues therapy; unequivocal progression or intolerable toxicity triggers the next line.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and staging
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation of a suspected or confirmed renal mass before deciding on a management pathway.
bullets: History, physical, performance status; screen for a hereditary syndrome (VHL, hereditary papillary) if young or multifocal
Labs: CBC, LDH, corrected calcium, LFTs, renal function, urinalysis
Contrast CT or MRI of the abdomen and pelvis to characterize the mass and nodes; chest CT for staging
Biopsy the renal mass when it changes management (small mass, ablation candidate, suspected non-clear-cell, or before systemic therapy)
Confirm histology and grade (clear-cell vs non-clear-cell); note any sarcomatoid or rhabdoid features

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: Clinical presentation
nodes.description: Management is defined first by disease extent and histology. Choose the current clinical picture.

options.label: Advanced clear-cell, progressed on prior systemic therapy

nodes.name: Localized stage
nodes.title: Localized RCC: stage / tumor extent
nodes.description: Stratify localized disease by primary tumor size and extent. This drives nephron-sparing vs radical surgery and the later adjuvant decision.

tables.title: Simplified AJCC-style T staging (renal cell carcinoma)
rows: Confined to kidney, 4 cm or less

options.label: Small renal mass (cT1a, 4 cm or less)

nodes.name: Small renal mass
nodes.title: Small renal mass (cT1a): management choice
nodes.description: For a small renal mass, nephron-sparing approaches are preferred; observation is reasonable in selected patients.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Localized / Small mass
bullets: Partial nephrectomy is preferred to preserve renal function when technically feasible
Thermal ablation for smaller masses or poor surgical candidates
Active surveillance for frail patients or limited life expectancy, with serial imaging

nodes.name: Partial nephrectomy
nodes.title: cT1a: partial nephrectomy
nodes.description: Nephron-sparing resection for a small renal mass; fully resected cT1a needs no adjuvant therapy and enters surveillance.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Localized / Partial nephrectomy
bullets: Partial nephrectomy (open, laparoscopic, or robotic) to negative margins
Preserves renal function versus radical nephrectomy for small masses
No adjuvant systemic therapy for fully resected cT1a
Enter risk-adapted surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Ablation
nodes.title: cT1a: thermal ablation
nodes.description: Image-guided ablation for a small mass or a poor surgical candidate.
bullets: Cryoablation or radiofrequency ablation for masses generally under 3 cm
Confirm histology by biopsy before or at ablation
Higher local recurrence than surgery; enter close imaging follow-up (next step)

nodes.name: Active surveillance
nodes.title: cT1a: active surveillance
nodes.description: Serial imaging for a small mass in a frail patient or one with limited life expectancy.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Localized / Active surveillance
bullets: Serial cross-sectional imaging (e.g. every 3-6 months initially, then annually)
Intervene on rapid growth, a size threshold, or patient preference
Consider biopsy to confirm histology and inform the threshold

nodes.name: Radical nephrectomy
nodes.title: Larger / locally advanced: nephrectomy
nodes.description: Radical (or partial where feasible) nephrectomy for larger or locally advanced disease, then post-operative pathology review.
bullets: Radical nephrectomy for larger, central, or locally advanced tumors; regional lymphadenectomy for clinically involved nodes
Partial nephrectomy where feasible to preserve function (e.g. solitary kidney, CKD)
Resect a tumor thrombus (renal vein / IVC) with the appropriate surgical approach
Review final pathology to assign recurrence risk (next step)

nodes.name: Post-operative risk
nodes.title: Post-nephrectomy pathology: recurrence risk
nodes.description: Assign recurrence risk on final pathology to decide whether to consider adjuvant therapy.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Localized / Post-op risk

tables.title: Higher-risk resected clear-cell features
rows: pT2 grade 4 or with sarcomatoid features
M1 with no evidence of disease after metastasectomy

nodes.name: Adjuvant decision
nodes.title: Resected higher-risk clear-cell: adjuvant therapy
nodes.description: For resected clear-cell RCC at increased risk of recurrence, adjuvant pembrolizumab is an option; weigh against immune toxicity.
bullets: Adjuvant pembrolizumab for about 1 year in eligible higher-risk resected clear-cell RCC
TKI adjuvant therapy is not routinely recommended (marginal, inconsistent benefit)
Shared decision: absolute risk reduction versus immune-related adverse events

nodes.name: Adjuvant pembrolizumab
nodes.title: Adjuvant pembrolizumab (about 1 year)
nodes.description: Adjuvant checkpoint inhibition for resected higher-risk clear-cell RCC.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Localized / Adjuvant pembrolizumab
bullets: Pembrolizumab for approximately 1 year in eligible resected higher-risk clear-cell disease
Baseline and on-treatment thyroid, adrenal, hepatic, and glucose monitoring
Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks (about 17 cycles) regimen referenced below
Enter surveillance on completion (next step)

nodes.name: Observation
nodes.title: Post-nephrectomy observation
nodes.description: Surveillance after resection for lower-risk disease or when adjuvant therapy is declined.
bullets: Risk-adapted imaging and labs after resection
No adjuvant systemic therapy
Enter the recurrence pathway if disease returns (next step)

nodes.name: Metastatic workup
nodes.title: Metastatic clear-cell: pre-treatment assessment
nodes.description: Before first-line systemic therapy, confirm histology and consider the role of surgery and metastasis-directed therapy.
bullets: Confirm clear-cell histology; note sarcomatoid features (favor IO-based therapy)
Cytoreductive nephrectomy for selected good-performance-status, low-burden patients; not routine when prompt systemic therapy is needed
Metastasis-directed therapy (metastasectomy or SBRT) for oligometastatic disease
Assess performance status and organ function for IO / TKI eligibility

nodes.name: IMDC risk
nodes.title: Advanced clear-cell: IMDC risk stratification
nodes.description: First-line therapy is guided by IMDC risk category. Count the six prognostic factors.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / IMDC risk

tables.title: IMDC risk model
rows: Time from diagnosis to systemic therapy

nodes.name: Favorable-risk first line
nodes.title: Favorable-risk clear-cell: first-line choice
nodes.description: For favorable-risk disease, an IO+TKI combination or TKI monotherapy are reasonable; dual IO is an option but its benefit is less established here.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Favorable / First line
bullets: IO+TKI combination (e.g. axitinib+pembrolizumab, lenvatinib+pembrolizumab, cabozantinib+nivolumab) for a high response rate
TKI monotherapy for patients preferring an oral single agent or with contraindications to IO
Dual IO (nivolumab+ipilimumab) is an option but favorable-risk benefit is less established

nodes.name: Intermediate/poor first line
nodes.title: Intermediate / poor-risk clear-cell: first-line choice
nodes.description: For intermediate/poor-risk disease, dual IO or an IO+TKI combination are preferred first-line; TKI monotherapy is an alternative.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Intermediate-poor / First line
bullets: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (dual IO) - durable responses, category 1
IO+TKI combination - high response rate, useful when prompt disease control is needed
TKI monotherapy (cabozantinib preferred) if IO is contraindicated

nodes.name: Nivolumab + ipilimumab
nodes.title: First-line: nivolumab + ipilimumab
nodes.description: Dual checkpoint blockade for advanced clear-cell RCC, then response assessment.
bullets: Induction nivolumab + ipilimumab, then nivolumab maintenance
Monitor for immune-related adverse events; have a steroid taper plan
Preferred for intermediate/poor-risk; less established for favorable-risk
Reassess response before deciding to continue or switch (next step)

nodes.name: IO + TKI combination
nodes.title: First-line: IO + TKI combination
nodes.description: Checkpoint inhibitor plus an anti-angiogenic TKI, then response assessment.
bullets: Options include axitinib+pembrolizumab, lenvatinib+pembrolizumab, or cabozantinib+nivolumab
High objective response rate; useful when prompt disease control is needed
Overlapping toxicity: distinguish TKI effects (hypertension, diarrhea, hand-foot) from immune effects
Regimen options referenced below: axitinib+pembrolizumab, lenvatinib+pembrolizumab, cabozantinib+nivolumab
Reassess response before deciding to continue or switch (next step)

nodes.name: TKI monotherapy
nodes.title: First-line: TKI monotherapy
nodes.description: Single-agent anti-angiogenic tyrosine-kinase inhibitor, then response assessment.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / TKI monotherapy
bullets: Cabozantinib, pazopanib, or sunitinib as an oral single agent
Cabozantinib is often preferred in intermediate/poor-risk disease
Reserve for IO-ineligible patients or a preference for oral monotherapy
Reassess response before deciding to continue or switch (next step)

nodes.name: First-line response
nodes.title: First-line: response assessment
nodes.description: Reassess disease on first-line therapy; response or durable stable disease continues therapy, unequivocal progression triggers second line.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / First-line response
bullets: Interval CT (RECIST-style) of chest/abdomen/pelvis at defined intervals
Distinguish immunotherapy pseudoprogression from true progression before switching
Manage toxicity; a treatment-limiting adverse event may also prompt a change

nodes.name: Continue first line
nodes.title: First-line response: continue therapy
nodes.description: Responding or stable disease continues first-line therapy with ongoing monitoring.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Continue first line
bullets: Continue the effective first-line regimen; consider a defined immunotherapy duration if on IO
Ongoing imaging and toxicity surveillance
Switch to second line at confirmed progression or intolerance (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line choice
nodes.title: Second-line: therapy selection
nodes.description: Second-line therapy switches mechanism where possible, guided by the first-line class already used.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Second line
bullets: After IO-based first line: an anti-angiogenic TKI (cabozantinib has robust data)
After TKI-only first line and IO-naive: single-agent nivolumab, or an alternate TKI
Switch class rather than repeat a regimen that already failed

nodes.name: Cabozantinib (second line)
nodes.title: Second-line: cabozantinib
nodes.description: Anti-angiogenic / MET-AXL TKI after prior IO-based therapy, then response assessment.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Cabozantinib second-line
bullets: Cabozantinib single agent after IO-based first line
Active against bone metastases; monitor blood pressure, diarrhea, hand-foot syndrome
Reassess response before deciding on later-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Nivolumab (second line)
nodes.title: Second-line: nivolumab monotherapy
nodes.description: Single-agent checkpoint inhibitor after TKI-only first line, then response assessment.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Nivolumab second-line
bullets: Nivolumab monotherapy for patients who received TKI-only first line and are IO-naive
Monitor for immune-related adverse events
Nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks (or 480 mg every 4 weeks) regimen referenced below
Reassess response before deciding on later-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Alternate TKI (second line)
nodes.title: Second-line: alternate TKI
nodes.description: A different anti-angiogenic TKI than used first line, then response assessment.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Alternate TKI second-line
bullets: Switch to a TKI not used first line (e.g. pazopanib or sunitinib after cabozantinib)
Monitor blood pressure, hand-foot syndrome, hepatic and thyroid function
Reassess response before deciding on later-line therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Second-line response
nodes.title: Second-line: response assessment
nodes.description: Reassess disease on second-line therapy; response or durable stable disease continues, progression triggers later-line therapy.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Second-line response
bullets: Interval imaging (RECIST-style) to classify response versus progression
Weigh cumulative toxicity and performance status against continued treatment
Confirmed progression or intolerance moves to later-line options

nodes.name: Continue second line
nodes.title: Second-line response: continue therapy
nodes.description: Responding or stable disease continues second-line therapy with ongoing monitoring.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Continue second line
bullets: Continue the effective second-line regimen with imaging and toxicity surveillance
Reduce or interrupt the dose for toxicity rather than switch prematurely where feasible
Move to later-line therapy at confirmed progression (next step)

nodes.name: Later-line choice
nodes.title: Later line: therapy selection
nodes.description: After IO and anti-angiogenic therapy, choose a HIF-2-alpha inhibitor, a TKI + mTOR combination, or best supportive care.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Later line
bullets: Belzutifan (HIF-2-alpha inhibitor) after both a checkpoint inhibitor and an anti-angiogenic agent
Lenvatinib + everolimus as an alternate later-line combination
Best supportive care / clinical trial when performance status is poor or options are exhausted

nodes.name: Belzutifan
nodes.title: Later line: belzutifan (HIF-2-alpha inhibitor)
nodes.description: Oral HIF-2-alpha inhibitor after progression on IO and anti-angiogenic therapy.
bullets: Belzutifan for advanced clear-cell RCC after both a checkpoint inhibitor and an anti-angiogenic agent
Class-specific anemia and hypoxia; monitor hemoglobin and oxygen saturation
Belzutifan 120 mg once daily regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Lenvatinib + everolimus
nodes.title: Later line: lenvatinib + everolimus
nodes.description: TKI plus mTOR inhibitor after IO and anti-angiogenic therapy.
bullets: Lenvatinib + everolimus as a later-line combination
Overlapping toxicity: fatigue, diarrhea, stomatitis, hyperglycemia, pneumonitis (everolimus)
Everolimus dosing referenced below; lenvatinib has no dedicated dose protocol here yet

nodes.name: Supportive care
nodes.title: Best supportive care / clinical trial
nodes.description: For poor performance status or exhausted systemic options.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Metastatic / Supportive care
bullets: Best supportive and palliative care; symptom-directed radiation for painful sites
Bone-modifying agent for bone metastases
Clinical trial where available and appropriate

nodes.name: Non-clear-cell workup
nodes.title: Metastatic non-clear-cell RCC: workup
nodes.description: Confirm the non-clear-cell subtype and test for actionable alterations before selecting therapy; prefer a clinical trial.

tables.title: Non-clear-cell subtypes and typical systemic approach

nodes.name: Non-clear-cell subtype
nodes.title: Metastatic non-clear-cell RCC: subtype
nodes.description: Non-clear-cell RCC is heterogeneous; a clinical trial is preferred. Select the histologic subtype.

nodes.name: Papillary
nodes.title: Papillary RCC: cabozantinib
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for metastatic papillary RCC, then progression assessment.
bullets: Cabozantinib preferred (superior to sunitinib in papillary disease)
IO+TKI combinations and clinical trials are reasonable alternatives
Test for MET alterations to inform targeted options
Reassess at progression (next step)

nodes.name: Chromophobe
nodes.title: Chromophobe RCC: TKI / mTOR options
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for metastatic chromophobe RCC, then progression assessment.
bullets: Lenvatinib + everolimus or a TKI; chromophobe is relatively angiogenesis-driven and less IO-responsive
Everolimus dosing referenced below; lenvatinib has no dedicated dose protocol here yet
Clinical trial preferred where available
Reassess at progression (next step)

nodes.name: Medullary / collecting-duct
nodes.title: Collecting-duct / medullary RCC: platinum chemotherapy
nodes.description: Aggressive histologies treated like urothelial-type carcinoma, then progression assessment.
bullets: Platinum-based cytotoxic chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine + platinum), treated like urothelial carcinoma
Medullary carcinoma associates with sickle-cell trait; confirm and counsel
Aggressive course - prioritize a clinical trial; gemcitabine + cisplatin regimen referenced below
Reassess at progression (next step)

nodes.name: Sarcomatoid / unclassified
nodes.title: Sarcomatoid-predominant / unclassified: IO-based therapy
nodes.description: Sarcomatoid features respond preferentially to checkpoint blockade, then progression assessment.
bullets: IO-based therapy (dual IO or IO+TKI) - sarcomatoid disease is preferentially IO-responsive
Monitor for immune-related adverse events
Nivolumab + ipilimumab regimen referenced below
Reassess at progression (next step)

nodes.name: Non-clear-cell progression
nodes.title: Non-clear-cell RCC: progression assessment
nodes.description: Reassess disease on non-clear-cell therapy; response continues, progression moves to a later-line switch.
bullets: Interval imaging to classify response versus progression
Switch mechanism at progression (TKI to IO-based, or vice versa)
Re-offer a clinical trial at each decision point

nodes.name: Continue non-clear-cell therapy
nodes.title: Non-clear-cell: continue therapy
nodes.description: Responding or stable non-clear-cell disease continues therapy with ongoing monitoring.
bullets: Continue the effective regimen with imaging and toxicity surveillance
Manage dose for tolerability rather than switch prematurely where feasible
Switch at confirmed progression (later-line option)

nodes.name: Non-clear-cell later line
nodes.title: Non-clear-cell: later-line switch
nodes.description: Later-line therapy after progression on first-line non-clear-cell treatment.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Non-clear-cell / Later line
bullets: Switch class: an anti-angiogenic TKI (e.g. cabozantinib) after IO-based first line, or IO-based therapy after a TKI
Everolimus-based combinations for a further later line
Prioritize a clinical trial; cabozantinib regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Recurrence
nodes.title: Recurrence after nephrectomy: pattern
nodes.description: Restage on recurrence; management differs for isolated local/oligometastatic disease versus widespread metastasis.
bullets: Restage with cross-sectional imaging of chest / abdomen / pelvis
Biopsy if the diagnosis or histology is uncertain
Re-establish IMDC risk before starting systemic therapy

nodes.name: Local / oligometastatic recurrence
nodes.title: Local / oligometastatic recurrence: metastasis-directed therapy
nodes.description: Isolated or limited recurrence amenable to local control, then response assessment.
bullets: Metastasectomy or SBRT for isolated / oligometastatic recurrence
May defer systemic therapy after complete local control, with close surveillance
Reassess after local therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Post-local-therapy assessment
nodes.title: Local recurrence: post-treatment assessment
nodes.description: After metastasis-directed therapy, decide between surveillance for controlled disease and systemic therapy for further progression.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Recurrence / Post-local assessment
bullets: Controlled disease can enter close surveillance and defer systemic therapy
New or progressive metastases move to the systemic (metastatic) pathway
Re-stratify IMDC risk before starting systemic therapy

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Risk-adapted follow-up after definitive local therapy; escalate on recurrence.
bullets: History, exam, labs, and cross-sectional imaging on a risk-adapted schedule (more frequent for higher stage)
Chest and abdominal imaging to detect the common lung and local recurrences
Monitor renal function, especially after partial nephrectomy or in CKD
A confirmed recurrence enters the recurrence pathway
